request.description: Establish the compiled physical control and hold-semantics baseline before selecting a learned-policy direction.
request.rationale: No candidate policy or development evidence exists. The initial decision is whether the 98% complete-hold objective is first limited by compiled torque authority, inertia/damping, singular-start timing, contact, or sampled-versus-continuous hold semantics, versus a learning/policy limitation. The PI-owned laboratory measurement records compiled model facts, deterministic torque-step and free-decay responses, and every 0.002 s state during held controls, while the accompanying independent check guards the measurement against kinematic, reset/update, and tolerance-analysis defects. These results can change whether the next work should be control-aware method development or learned-policy training/diagnosis; they do not claim policy performance or official success.

request.candidates_and_roles: No training candidates have been produced. Working, best-known, and retained roles are empty.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One completed startup measurement operation (M1) containing two PI-owned Python-module measurements: an executed verification and a compiled-dynamics trace artifact. No training steps and no candidate artifacts.
request.current_goal_gap: No learned candidate exists and no development success rate has been measured. The remaining gap is capability evidence for a policy that can reach arbitrary official targets, brake the torque-driven arm, and sustain the complete hold with sufficient margin for the 98% objective.
request.current_synthesis: Observed evidence from completed M1: the independent verification passed analytic planar forward kinematics (maximum error 2.78e-17 m), zero-action zero-velocity invariance over 40 internal updates, repeated held-control traces with 30 samples and 29 changing updates per reset, and detection of two deliberately constructed interior tolerance excursions that boundary-only sampling would miss. The operative compiled model measured nq=nv=nu=2, timestep 0.002 s, 10 internal steps per 20 ms control interval, diagonal free-space dof_M0 values 0.01210 and 0.01019, damping and armature 0.5 and 0.01, gear 5, control range [-1,1], and no actuator force limit. In deterministic held unit-torque traces, joint speeds reached about 9.6-9.7 rad/s within 80 ms; zero-action decay from [0.8,-0.5] rad/s reduced to [0.0133,-0.0030] rad/s over 100 ms; tested traces had zero contacts. These observations support the interpretation that motion authority is ample and that overshoot/braking and hold robustness are more consequential initial mechanisms than inability to reach. The near-tolerance controlled trace reached a minimum of 8.5 mm but exceeded 10 mm at both control boundaries and at 28 internal samples, demonstrating that the tested trajectory was not a successful hold and that sampled and internal behavior can differ. Competing explanation A, a compiled-dynamics authority bottleneck, is weakened for the tested configurations but not excluded across all target geometry or policy routes. Explanation B, a learned-policy timing/braking/hold bottleneck, is now the leading development hypothesis, but it is untested because no policy was evaluated. Continuous protected evaluator semantics remain unknown; the synthetic check validates only the analysis capability, not the hidden evaluator.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether the first capability intervention should develop a learned policy under the existing torque interface with explicit braking/hold-sensitive diagnostics, or whether a broader physical route/contact/geometry investigation is needed first. Evidence that would redirect away from policy development would include target- or branch-conditioned torque-step failures, contact impulses, actuator saturation/force behavior inconsistent with the compiled facts, or systematic inability to settle even under a competent feedback trajectory. Evidence that would support policy-focused development would be a candidate that reaches targets but loses the hold, shows high near-tolerance qdot or internal excursions, or fails by target geometry while the compiled model remains contact-free and dynamically authoritative. The official evaluator's continuous-versus-boundary rule is still unavailable, so any development candidate must be judged with internal traces or conservative margin rather than aggregate sampled success alone.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 196 successful episodes out of 200, where each success requires entering the 1 cm target ball and remaining continuously within it for 2 seconds. M1 directly established the physical control and sampling conditions that a learned policy must satisfy; it did not measure policy success.
request.next_direction_or_closure: M1 establishes the initial scientific direction: prioritize learned-policy capability development and mechanism-level evaluation of braking and hold robustness, rather than treating reachability or static actuation authority as the first bottleneck. This is a provisional direction because policy behavior and protected hold semantics remain unmeasured. Goal review should decide whether to open the bounded policy-capability inquiry.
request.next_question: At the next goal review, determine whether to open a bounded inquiry on developing and measuring a learned policy for torque-aware reach, braking, and complete-hold robustness under the official target distribution, using M1's compiled dynamics and internal-step distinction as the mechanism baseline.

request.closure_condition: Close when completed development evidence supports a bounded conclusion about this policy route: either a measured candidate is sufficiently capable and selected for goal review, or measured failures and mechanism diagnostics identify a consequential limitation or redirect. The evidence must include candidate-level task success and mechanism-relevant diagnostics for the selected artifact, including first reach, uninterrupted hold, target-geometry/branch conditioning, near-tolerance velocity or action, contacts, and internal-step behavior where available; unresolved protected evaluator semantics remain an explicit limitation rather than being treated as settled.
request.goal_connection: The campaign has no learned candidate and therefore no evidence of the capability required for at least 196 successes in the protected 200-episode assessment. This inquiry will produce and measure candidate policies on the official target distribution, distinguishing reach failure, braking/settling failure, branch or geometry effects, contacts, and internal-step tolerance excursions so that progress toward the 98% goal is not inferred from reward or boundary-only success.
request.question: Develop and measure a learned policy for torque-aware reach, braking, and complete-hold robustness under the official target distribution, using M1's compiled dynamics and internal-step distinction as the mechanism baseline.
request.rationale: Opening is justified over official assessment because no candidate exists, no best-known role can support commitment, and M1 measured only compiled dynamics and a synthetic internal-step distinction. M1 weakens a generic authority bottleneck but does not test a learned policy, so the highest-value bounded work is to develop and measure the method under the existing torque interface. A candidate that reaches but loses the hold would support policy-control development; systematic target/branch torque-step or contact failures, or inability to settle under a competent route, would redirect the campaign toward the corresponding physical or implementation mechanism. The inquiry does not assume either explanation and will preserve recipe-specific limits.

request.candidates_and_roles: No training candidates have been produced. Working, best-known, and retained roles are empty. The inquiry will select complete measured artifacts only after development evidence is available; training proxies alone will not establish development performance or official success.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One completed startup measurement operation (M1) and one completed inquiry-opening event (E2); no training steps, candidate artifacts, or development evaluations have been produced in this inquiry.
request.current_goal_gap: No learned policy has been trained or measured. The remaining capability gap is evidence that one policy can reach the full official target distribution, brake the torque-driven arm, and sustain the complete hold with adequate robustness, including behavior between 20 ms control boundaries if that distinction matters to the protected evaluator.
request.current_synthesis: Observed M1 evidence: independent analytic planar forward-kinematics verification passed with maximum error 2.78e-17 m; zero action with zero velocity remained invariant over 40 internal updates; repeated held-control traces changed over 29 of 30 samples after reset; the compiled model had nq=nv=nu=2, a 0.002 s internal timestep, 10 internal steps per 20 ms action, diagonal free-space dof_M0 values 0.01210 and 0.01019, damping and armature 0.5 and 0.01, gear 5, control range [-1,1], and no actuator force limit; held unit-torque traces reached approximately 9.6-9.7 rad/s within 80 ms; zero-action decay reduced [0.8,-0.5] rad/s to [0.0133,-0.0030] rad/s over 100 ms; and the tested traces had zero contacts. A near-tolerance controlled trace reached 8.5 mm but exceeded 10 mm at both control boundaries and at 28 internal samples, showing that the tested trajectory was not a successful hold and that boundary-only checks can miss interior excursions. These observations weaken a generic motion-authority bottleneck for the tested configurations, but do not exclude target- or route-conditioned limitations. They also support braking and hold robustness as consequential mechanisms to test. Correction to the inherited interpretation: policy timing/braking/hold failure is a leading development hypothesis, not an established learned-policy explanation, because M1 evaluated deterministic plant traces and no policy. The absence of a candidate, candidate diagnostics, and protected continuous-hold semantics remains decisive uncertainty. No strongest candidate exists; official assessment is therefore not justified.
request.decision_frontier: The active distinction is whether a learned policy under the existing torque interface can convert the measured plant authority into robust reach-and-hold behavior, or whether failures reveal a consequential physical or route-conditioned limitation requiring a different direction. Candidate-level success and diagnostics that show reaching with unstable holds, high near-tolerance qdot/action, internal tolerance excursions, or geometry/branch-conditioned deficits would support targeted policy/control development. Target- or branch-conditioned torque-step failure, recurrent contact impulses, actuator behavior inconsistent with M1, or failure to settle under a competent feedback trajectory would redirect investigation toward the corresponding physical or implementation mechanism. The official evaluator's sampled-versus-continuous rule remains unavailable; internal traces and conservative margin must therefore be preserved and not conflated with official certification.
request.human_goal_connection: The immutable goal is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes, with each success requiring entry into the 1 cm target ball and an uninterrupted 2 second hold. M1 established relevant plant and timing facts but produced no learned candidate, so the campaign currently has no artifact that can be committed to official assessment.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Open inquiry I1 and continue with bounded policy-capability development and mechanism-level measurement. This is preferred to official assessment because no explicit best-known learned candidate exists and M1 did not measure policy capability. The inquiry may close positively, negatively, or inconclusively once its stated candidate and diagnostic evidence is completed; closure itself will not certify the human goal.
request.next_question: Develop and measure a learned policy for torque-aware reach, braking, and complete-hold robustness under the official target distribution, using M1's compiled dynamics and internal-step distinction as the mechanism baseline.

request.description: Verify that the PI-owned training environment exposes the complete official target-radius distribution before producing the first I1 policy candidate.
request.rationale: The active inquiry concerns policy capability under the official 6–20 cm distribution. The prior training surface omitted all 6–14 cm targets, so training before correcting and checking this would produce an artifact whose exposure cannot answer the inquiry. This measurement tests the exact implementation change and does not claim policy performance.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO policy with the current torque-control recipe after aligning training target radii to the complete official 6–20 cm distribution.
request.rationale: M1 established bounded compiled-plant authority but no learned-policy capability, and M2 verified that the training environment now exposes the official radial range. A full-allocation fresh run is the highest-value next development action because it produces the first complete policy artifact whose later measurement can distinguish non-reaching, braking/settling, branch/geometry, and hold failures. This run is a recipe-specific development result; training proxies will not be treated as task success or as a privileged terminal checkpoint.
